reasoning: Both attempts pass every check and get the springs, the offset-based highlight glide and the mouse/touch press feedback right. B creates its slide spring outside the show, so it starts at the hidden offset and the slide-up is certain; reopening during the closing slide retargets the same mounted panel. A uses the show removal-delay and present pattern, but its slide spring starts at whatever present() returns when the picker is created, which risks no slide-up. Its fixed 0.4 s delay is also tight for the slide. B's dependence on the spring settling exactly is a smaller risk, since an unremoved panel is off screen and takes no clicks. B wins narrowly.

criteria.note: The `slideOffset`, highlight `position` and tile `scale` springs are all created in component bodies and bound to Position or Size; nothing is created inside a binding.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays / opening slides panel
criteria.note: `show(isBuildMode, function(_, present) ... , PICKER_EXIT_SECONDS)` keeps the picker in the tree until the slide-down ends and moves the panel's Position, not UIScale. But the spring starts at whatever `present()` returns when it is created, so the slide-up only plays if `present` starts false, and the 0.4 s delay is tight for a 0.35 s spring.

`Interactable = isShown` blocks clicks while closing, and show's delay or `present` pattern should reverse cleanly when reopened. This rests on show's internal handling rather than state the attempt controls itself.
The highlight sits in the padded panel at `UDim2.fromOffset((index - 1) * (TILE_SIZE + TILE_GAP), 0)`, all in offset units with no AbsolutePosition.
InputBegan/InputEnded for MouseButton1 and Touch drive `isPressed`, MouseLeave resets it, and keyboard activation gets an extra impulse.
All checks pass and selection, placement and scaling are kept. Adding `Vide.strict = RunService:IsStudio()` is an unrequested global change.
The `offset` spring is in the blockPicker body, and the ring and tile springs are made in the show builder or component bodies. No spring is created inside an effect or binding.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays / opening slides panel
criteria.note: The spring starts hidden because Open is false at startup and retargets to `SHOWN_OFFSET`. `isMounted = Open() or offset() ~= hiddenOffset` keeps the panel until it is off screen, and the slide moves Position.

Reopening mid-slide keeps the panel mounted and retargets the same spring, and `Interactable = props.Open` blocks clicks while closing. Removal depends on the spring settling exactly on `hiddenOffset`; if it never does, an invisible panel lingers, which is harmless.
`PANEL_PADDING - RING_OUTSET + (selectedIndex() - 1) * TILE_STRIDE` uses only offset units.
MouseButton1 and Touch set `isPressed` on InputBegan and clear it on InputEnded or MouseLeave, and a UIScale spring squashes the button.
All checks pass, and replacing UIPadding with an inset Tiles frame keeps the layout matched to the ring math.

strengths: Uses Vide's intended show removal-delay and present pattern
Clean offset math for the highlight
Press feedback for mouse and touch, plus an impulse for keyboard activation
weaknesses: The slide-up depends on `present` starting false; otherwise the panel pops in
The fixed 0.4 s exit delay is only loosely tied to the spring's settle time
Sets Vide.strict, which is out of scope

strengths: The slide-up is guaranteed because the spring lives outside show and starts hidden
Reopening mid-close retargets the same panel with no remount
The ring sits slightly outside the tile, so a squashed tile still reads as selected
weaknesses: Removal relies on the spring exactly equalling its target
Changes the BlockPicker API so the component handles its own show, a bit more coupling
